newsitem.title: CHINA: China steelmaker says it turns profitable.
newsitem.headline: China steelmaker says it turns profitable.

text.p: Anshan Iron and Steel Co, long seen as one of the problem firms in China's ailing state sector, recorded a net profit of 278 million yuan ($33 million) in the first 10 months of the year, the China Daily said on Saturday.

The newspaper quoted Wen Shizhen, governor of Liaoning province, as saying the company was now seen as a model for other state enterprises, demonstrating how a loss-making operation could be transformed into a profitable business.

The newspaper said Anshan, based in Liaoning province and one of China's major steel manufacturing facilities, lost 200 million yuan in the first half of last year. It gave no figure for the first 10 months of 1995.
While other Chinese steelmakers were able to sell shares to foreign investors, Anshan was studiously avoided by the foreign investment community.
The China Daily said that Anshan had taken tough measures to streamline its management and had undertaken major projects to upgrade its technology.
Liaoning province, a centre of heavy industry, has many state-run companies that are dependent on central government subsidies in order to stay in business.
The province has some 1,260 large or medium sized state-run companies, according to the newspaper.
It gave no figures for how many of them were losing money but central government officials have publicly expressed concern over financial problems in the province.

The China Daily also quoted Wen as saying that the Liaoyang Petrochemical Fibre Company was also being used as a model for the reform of state enterprises. It gave no details of the company's results, however.
